transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because my sleep has just been… awful for a long time. I come home so tired, like I could just drop, especially after being in people’s homes all day for work, and then I get in bed and it’s not real sleep. Every little noise in the house wakes me up—pipes, a car outside, whatever—and then I’m up before the alarm, just lying there feeling like I didn’t rest at all. It’s been wearing me down.
When you get into bed, how long does it usually take you to fall asleep?

It’s hard to say exactly… I mean, I get into bed already exhausted, like my body is done, so sometimes I think I should just knock out. But the sleep is so broken. I’ll start to drift, and then a little sound in the house will pull me right back up—like the pipes or something outside. Then before I know it I’m awake way too early, before the alarm, feeling like I never really slept at all.
Once you fall asleep, do you have trouble staying asleep, or do you wake up multiple times during the night?

Yeah, I do wake up a lot. It’s like once I’m asleep, it doesn’t really stay that way. Every little noise in the house gets me—the pipes, a car going by, sometimes I don’t even know what it was. I’ll be lying there thinking I should be resting because I was so tired when I got into bed, and then I’m just… awake again. And then I’m up before the alarm anyway, feeling like I never really slept.
When you wake up before your alarm, are you able to fall back asleep, or do you feel wide awake and unable to get back to sleep?

Usually I can’t really get back to sleep. I’ll be up before the alarm and just lie there, and it’s frustrating because I went to bed so exhausted. It’s like my sleep is broken all night anyway—every little sound in the house wakes me up, the pipes or a car outside—and by the time morning comes I feel like I never really rested.
Even when you are able to sleep for a few hours, do you still wake up feeling unrefreshed or like you haven’t truly rested?

Yes… that’s exactly it. Even if I do get a few hours, it doesn’t feel like real sleep. I wake up before the alarm and I’m already tired, like I never actually rested. It’s been going on a long time—falling into bed exhausted, then waking up at every little sound in the house. Even the little creaks and things, and then by morning I’m just… worn out.
Even when there aren’t any noises or interruptions, do you still wake up feeling like you didn’t rest properly?

Yeah… even when it’s quiet, I still wake up like I didn’t really sleep right. I mean, the noises make it worse, but it’s not only that. I can fall into bed completely wiped out, and somehow I’m still up before the alarm feeling like I’ve been half-awake all night. Sometimes I’ll start thinking about how I have to get moving for the day, and then I’m just lying there annoyed, because it’s like… what was the point of sleeping if I still feel this tired?
Even when you're in a completely quiet environment, do you still wake up feeling like you haven't rested properly?

Yes… yes, even if it’s totally quiet, I still wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest. I keep thinking maybe it’s the little sounds in the house, because honestly every creak or car outside seems to wake me up, and then I get annoyed about it. But even without that, I’ll fall into bed so tired and still be up before the alarm like I’ve only been half-asleep. It’s been going on a long time.
During the day, do you ever feel so tired that you have trouble staying awake, like you might fall asleep even during activities like driving or talking to someone?

Not like I’m falling asleep while talking to someone, no… at least I don’t think so. But I do get really worn down. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and then come back and help with things at home, my whole body just feels heavy. Even sitting down to do my charting notes, or trying to fold laundry, it feels like too much to push through sometimes. Like I’m awake, but I’m dragging myself through it.
Even when you have plenty of time to sleep and nothing is interrupting you, does your sleep still feel unrefreshing or like you haven't truly rested?

Yeah… that’s pretty much what it feels like. Even if I technically have enough hours, I fall into bed exhausted and still wake up like I didn’t really sleep. I’m really sensitive to every little sound in the house too—like a door creaking or something outside—and then I’m up before the alarm anyway. It’s frustrating, because I’m supposed to feel rested, but I just don’t.
Even when you have enough time to sleep and your environment is ideal—like no interruptions, quiet, and comfortable—does your sleep still feel unrefreshing or like you haven’t truly rested?

Yes… even if everything is quiet and I’ve got time to sleep, I still wake up like I didn’t really rest. I mean, I’m already falling into bed exhausted most nights, and then it’s like every tiny sound in the house catches me—my house makes these little creaks, and I’ll start thinking, “What was that?”—but even when it’s not that, I’m up before the alarm and I feel like I was never fully asleep. It’s been going on so long that I almost expect it now.
Even when you have enough time to sleep and your environment is ideal—like no interruptions, quiet, and comfortable—does your sleep still feel unrefreshing or like you haven’t truly rested?

Yeah… I know I already said it, but yes. That’s kind of why I’m here, honestly. My sleep has been broken for a long time—like I fall into bed just completely exhausted, and then every little sound in the house wakes me up. The house creaks, or I hear something outside, and I’m suddenly alert.

And then I’m awake before the alarm anyway, feeling like I never really got real rest. It’s not just one bad night, it’s been this ongoing thing.

Even when you have enough time to sleep and your environment is completely ideal—like no interruptions, total quiet, and you’re comfortable—does your sleep still feel unrefreshing, like you haven’t truly rested?

Yes… I know I’m kind of repeating myself, but that’s exactly it. I’m here because my sleep has just been broken for so long. I’ll fall into bed totally exhausted, and then it’s like I’m half-listening all night—every little sound in the house wakes me up. And then I’m up before the alarm anyway, feeling like I never really rested.

It’s funny, I used to think maybe it was just the house making noises, or the neighbors, or needing a better pillow, you know? I’ve tried changing little things like that. But even when things are quiet and I should be comfortable, I still wake up feeling like I didn’t get real sleep.
